rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protection Ordinance – just cause for termination
rules.requirement: Landlords may terminate a covered tenancy only for an enumerated at-fault or no-fault just cause. The termination notice must state the cause, and curable lease violations require a prior written notice with an opportunity to cure. Owner move-in under leases entered on or after June 24, 2023 is allowed only with the tenant's written agreement or a lease provision permitting it. Substantial-remodel evictions require posted applications, secured permits and a detailed sworn notice.
rules.key_value: At-fault or no-fault just cause required
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies (lawful occupancy over 30 days) in residential rental property in the City of San Diego, including rented dwellings in mobilehome parks. Fixed-term leases of 3 months or less are not covered.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels; occupancies of 30 days or less; deed- or regulatory-restricted affordable housing and subsidized affordable housing (Section 8 voucher tenants remain covered); MRL mobilehomes; nonprofit hospital, religious, care and transitional housing; school dormitories; units where the tenant shares a kitchen or bath with an owner-occupant; owner-occupied single-family homes renting no more than 2 units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplexes; separately alienable units not owned by a REIT, corporation or corporate-member LLC, where written exemption notice was given; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Separately alienable units (e.g., condos, single-family homes) are exempt only if the owner is not a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member AND written exemption notice was given to the tenant. Excludes deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing, tenancies of 30 days or less, fixed-term leases of 3 months or less, and shared kitchen/bath with an owner-occupant.

rules.penalty: Tenant may sue for injunctive and equitable relief and money damages, including punitive damages. Wrongful eviction carries damages of at least 3x actual economic damages, plus attorney's fees in non-unlawful-detainer actions. A violation is an affirmative defense in an unlawful detainer action.
rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7 (§ 98.0701 et seq.)
rules.quoted_span: The purpose of the Ordinance is to require Just Cause for termination of residential tenancies consistent with California Civil Code section 1946.2, to limit the reasons for termination of a residential tenancy, to require greater tenant relocation assistance in specified circumstances and to provide additional tenant protections.
rules.conflict_note: Secondary legal-aid FAQ last updated September 21, 2023. Subsequent amendments as of 2026-10-01 cannot be verified from this source.

rules.title: San Diego no-fault relocation assistance
rules.requirement: For no-fault terminations, the landlord must pay relocation assistance equal to 2 months of actual rent, either by direct payment within 15 days of the notice or by waiving the final months' rent. The amount rises to 3 months for senior (62+) or disabled tenants, regardless of income or length of tenancy.
rules.key_value: 2 months' rent; 3 months' rent for seniors 62+ or disabled tenants
rules.coverage_conditions: No-fault terminations of covered tenancies under the San Diego Tenant Protection Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as the Ordinance. No assistance is owed if a government agency or court finds the tenant at fault for a habitability-vacate condition.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Separately alienable units are exempt only if the owner is not a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member AND written exemption notice was given. Excludes deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing.

rules.penalty: Landlord is liable for at least 3x the required relocation assistance plus actual economic damages.
rules.quoted_span: The Landlord must provide Relocation Assistance to the Tenants in one of the following ways: A direct payment equal to two (2) months of the actual rent (contract rent) OR Waive in writing or not collect two (2) months of the actual rent (contract rent).
rules.conflict_note: Secondary FAQ from 2023. Amendments since then are unverified.

rules.title: San Diego right of first offer after no-fault eviction
rules.requirement: If a unit is re-offered for rent within 5 years of a no-fault eviction, the landlord must first offer it in writing to the displaced tenant, provided the tenant requested an offer in writing within 30 days of the termination notice and gave contact information. Failure to comply voids the termination notice.
rules.coverage_conditions: No-fault terminations of covered tenancies, other than withdrawal from the rental market.
rules.exemptions: Withdrawal from the rental market; Ordinance exemptions.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenant must have requested the offer in writing within 30 days of the termination notice and provided a mailing or email address. Ordinance exemptions also apply.

rules.title: San Diego notice of residential tenant protections
rules.requirement: Owners of covered property must give tenants a prescribed written notice of rent cap and just-cause protections in at least 12-point type, together with SDHC's Tenant Protection Guide. For new or renewed tenancies the notice must be a lease addendum or a tenant-signed notice; existing tenancies had to receive it by September 22, 2023.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies in residential rental property subject to the Ordinance.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Ordinance exemptions apply, including owner-type plus exemption-notice conditions and affordable-housing exclusions.

rules.title: San Diego requirement to file termination notices with SDHC
rules.requirement: Landlords must file a copy of at-fault and no-fault termination notices with the San Diego Housing Commission within 3 business days of serving the tenant. The requirement takes effect 30 days after SDHC publicly announces its submission portal.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Effective only 30 days after SDHC publicly notices its submission portal. Ordinance exemptions apply.

rules.quoted_span: The Landlord must provide written notice to SDHC no later than 3 business days after the date the landlord provided the notice to tenant. This does not apply until 30 days after SDHC establishes a submission portal and provides the public notice of its creation.
rules.conflict_note: The 2023 FAQ marks this 'CURRENTLY NOT IN EFFECT' and estimates a July 2024 portal launch. If the portal launched, the requirement may be in force as of 2026-10-01; this is unverified.

rules.title: San Diego tenant buyout agreement requirements
rules.requirement: Before making a buyout offer, landlords must give tenants prescribed written disclosures. Buyout agreements must be in writing, include bold 14-point rights statements, and be translated when negotiated in another language. Agreements for less than the applicable relocation assistance, or that waive Ordinance rights, are void.
rules.coverage_conditions: Buyout offers and agreements with tenants in covered tenancies.
rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7
rules.quoted_span: Buyout agreements for amounts less than the amount of relocation assistance available to Tenant is void.
